description: Sync monitors, dashboards, SLOs, notebooks and incidents from your Datadog organization, plus log, metric and SLO summaries. Only private incidents carry a Datadog restriction.
opening: Sync monitors with their runbook messages, dashboard summaries, SLO definitions, notebooks and incidents from one Datadog organization. Each is one document. Each sync also adds a log count for the sync window, and metric and SLO histories when you set their query or SLO id.

Raw logs, traces, metric points and dashboard widgets are not synced. Only incidents carry a Datadog restriction: with Enforce ACL on, a private incident is hidden from everyone, including its participants. Items deleted in Datadog can stay in HydraDB.

permissions.who_can_read: Only incidents carry a Datadog restriction. An incident Datadog marks private can be read by no one, not even its participants, because Datadog does not list them. Monitors, dashboards, SLOs, notebooks, log and metric summaries, and incidents visible to the organization follow the access rule you set on the resource. With no rule, everyone who can query the collection can read them.
permissions.identity: No people are read. A private incident is closed to everyone.
permissions.when_unreadable: If Datadog reports an incident visibility HydraDB does not recognise, HydraDB makes no permission claim for that incident. It follows the access rule you set on its resource. With no rule, everyone who can query the collection can read it.
notes: With Enforce ACL off, private incidents are searchable like any other item.

connect.auth: Datadog uses an API key and an application key. The application key's scopes decide what syncs.

credentials.name: api_key
credentials.text: A Datadog API key, from Organization Settings, API Keys. It identifies your org.

credentials.name: app_key
credentials.text: A Datadog application key, from Organization Settings, Application Keys. It is created without scopes, so edit it afterwards to add the scopes below.

settings.name: site
settings.text: Your Datadog site if it is not US1, for example `us5.datadoghq.com` or `datadoghq.eu`.

settings.name: log_query
settings.text: A full logs query to count. Takes priority over `log_service`.

settings.name: log_service
settings.text: One service name to narrow the log count. Ignored when `log_query` is set.

settings.name: log_measure
settings.text: A log measure to sum alongside the count, for example `@duration`.

settings.name: metric_query
settings.text: A metrics query to sync as a history. Leave it blank to skip metrics.

settings.name: slo_id_us
settings.text: An SLO id whose history to sync, labelled US. Every SLO id field reads from your configured site.

settings.name: slo_id_eu
settings.text: An SLO id whose history to sync, labelled EU.

settings.name: slo_id_ca
settings.text: An SLO id whose history to sync, labelled CA.

connect.permissions_label: Scopes to add to the application key

permissions.name: incident_read
permissions.text: if Datadog refuses it on the first request, incidents are skipped and everything else syncs.

connect.permissions_note: An application key left without scopes has its owner's full permissions. Set exactly these scopes. Most refused reads fail the sync.

steps.title: Create the keys
steps.text: In Datadog, create an API key under Organization Settings, API Keys, and an application key under Organization Settings, Application Keys.

steps.title: Scope the application key
steps.text: Open the new application key and edit its scopes to exactly the list above.

steps.title: Create the connector
steps.text: Paste the keys as `api_key` and `app_key`. Set `site` if your org is not on US1.

steps.title: Select All data
steps.text: There is nothing to browse. Select the single All data resource.

steps.title: Choose what to summarise
steps.text: Narrow the log count with `log_query` or `log_service`, and add `log_measure` for a sum. Left blank, logs are still counted across the default `main` index, normally as one total. Set `metric_query` and the SLO id fields to sync those histories. Left blank, they are skipped.

connect.account: One connector reads one Datadog organization on one site.

sync.first_sync: Monitors, dashboards, SLOs, notebooks and incidents are read in full, whatever their age. The log count, metric history and SLO history cover the window set by `lookback_days`, 30 days by default. Each metric or SLO history document covers the month up to one day, not that day alone.
sync.changes: Monitors, dashboards, SLOs, notebooks and incidents are read in full on every sync, and ones that did not change are skipped. Metric and SLO histories add documents as days pass. The log count is recalculated for each sync window.
sync.edits: A changed monitor, dashboard, SLO, notebook or incident updates its document on the next sync.
sync.deletes: Items deleted in Datadog can stay searchable in HydraDB. Dashboards Datadog has marked as deleted are not synced.
notes: A changed log count can become a new document instead of replacing the old one, so earlier counts can stay searchable.
An unknown metric can return an empty history.
If HydraDB cannot read every incident, the sync fails instead of keeping a partial list.

shared_attributes.name: additional_metadata.datadog_stream
shared_attributes.text: The kind of record: `monitors`, `dashboards`, `slos`, `notebooks`, `incidents`, `aggregate_logs`, `metric_response_time`, `slo_history_us_prod`, `slo_history_eu_prod` or `slo_history_ca_prod`. Keeps only monitors, only incidents, and so on. Not searchable.

shared_attributes.name: connector_id
shared_attributes.text: Limits a query to this connector's items. Not searchable.

shared_attributes.name: stream_type
shared_attributes.text: The kind of record, the same value as `additional_metadata.datadog_stream`.

documents.name: Monitors
documents.title: The monitor name, else `Datadog monitor`.
documents.text: The name, then `Type`, `Status`, `Priority`, `Query`, `Tags`, `Created by` and `Modified` lines, then the monitor message, usually the runbook, word for word. The title is searchable too.
documents.date: When the monitor was last modified.

attributes.name: Modified
attributes.text: When the monitor was last modified, written as the `Modified` line.

attributes.name: Service tags
attributes.text: Each `service:` tag links the monitor to that service, as `service:<name>`, together with the SLOs and incidents of the same service. The tags themselves are searchable in the `Tags` line. Not searchable as links.

attributes.name: Composite monitor query
attributes.text: A composite monitor links to each monitor in its query. Not searchable as links.

documents.name: Dashboards
documents.one_document: One dashboard summary, without its widgets.
documents.title: The dashboard title, else `Datadog dashboard`.
documents.date: When the dashboard was last modified.
documents.link_back: None. The dashboard's address is the searchable `URL` line.

attributes.name: Modified
attributes.text: When the dashboard was last modified, written as the `Modified` line.

documents.name: SLOs
documents.title: The SLO name, else `Datadog SLO`.
documents.text: The name, then `Description`, `Type`, `Timeframe`, the target or per-timeframe thresholds, the `Numerator` and `Denominator` queries, and `Tags`. The title is searchable too.
documents.date: When the SLO was last modified.

attributes.name: Monitors
attributes.text: Links the SLO to each monitor it is built on. Not searchable.

attributes.name: Service tags
attributes.text: Each `service:` tag links the SLO to that service, as `service:<name>`. Not searchable as links.

attributes.name: Modified
attributes.text: When the SLO was last modified. Not searchable.

documents.name: Notebooks
documents.one_document: One notebook with its markdown cells.
documents.title: The notebook name, else `Datadog notebook`.
documents.text: The name, then `Author`, `Status` and `Modified` lines, then the text of every markdown cell. Graph cells add nothing. The title is searchable too.
documents.date: When the notebook was last modified.

attributes.name: Modified
attributes.text: When the notebook was last modified, written as the `Modified` line.

documents.name: Incidents
documents.one_document: One declared incident, private ones included.
documents.title: The incident title, else `Datadog incident`.
documents.text: The title, then `Visibility`, `State`, `Severity`, `Customer impacted`, `Customer impact scope`, `Declared`, `Detected` and `Resolved` lines, and the incident's own fields, such as services and teams.
documents.date: When the incident was last modified.
documents.files: A postmortem notebook attached to the incident becomes a link to that notebook. Other attachments are not read.

attributes.name: visibility
attributes.text: `organization` or `private`, written as the `Visibility` line. With Enforce ACL on, a private incident is hidden from everyone.

attributes.name: Postmortem
attributes.text: Links the incident to its postmortem notebook. Not searchable as a link.

attributes.name: Services
attributes.text: Each service named on the incident links it to that service, as `service:<name>`. Not searchable as links.

attributes.name: Modified
attributes.text: When the incident was last modified. Not searchable.

documents.name: Log counts
documents.one_document: One log count for the sync window, usually a single total. Individual log messages are not synced.
documents.title: `Datadog log aggregate`, with the host and status added when present.
documents.text: `Host`, `Status` and `Count` lines, and the sum of `log_measure` when set. The title is searchable too.

attributes.name: host, status
attributes.text: The host and status the count is grouped by, in the title and text. Usually empty for the default total.

documents.name: Metric histories
documents.one_document: One window of `metric_query`. Only when `metric_query` is set.
documents.title: `Datadog metric:` followed by the metric or query.
documents.text: `Query` and `Window` lines, and one `Series` line per returned series with a summary of its points. The title is searchable too.

attributes.name: query, metric, window_start, window_end
attributes.text: The query, the metric name and the window. The window end is the result date.

documents.name: SLO histories
documents.one_document: One history window of an SLO id set in `slo_id_us`, `slo_id_eu` or `slo_id_ca`.
documents.title: A `Datadog SLO` history title with the SLO name.
documents.text: `SLO`, `Description`, `SLI Value`, `Target`, `Type`, `Tags`, `Creator`, `Window`, `Region` and `SLO Id` lines. The title is searchable too.

attributes.name: slo_id
attributes.text: The SLO id, written as the `SLO Id` line. Links the history window to the SLO's own record when it is synced.

attributes.name: sli_value, target, region
attributes.text: The measured value, the target and the region label. The region is a label only.

attributes.name: window_start, window_end
attributes.text: The history period, written as the `Window` line. The window end is the result date.

example_searches: What is the runbook for the checkout latency monitor?
Which SLOs are built on the api-errors monitor?
What did the on-call write in the database migration notebook?

connections: An SLO to each monitor it is built on.
A composite monitor to each monitor in its query.
An incident to its postmortem notebook.
An SLO history window to its SLO.
Monitors, SLOs and incidents to their service, from `service:` tags and incident service fields.
Dashboards are not linked to the monitors or SLOs they show, because widgets are not synced.
Links reach only items this connector has synced, that are not deleted. No links to items in other tools.
graph.people: No one is attached as a person in the graph. Monitor creators and dashboard and notebook authors appear only in the text.
graph.from_text: Monitor messages, notebook cells, descriptions and incident text.

not_synced: Raw logs, traces, events and metric points beyond the log count, `metric_query` and the SLO ids you set.
Incident timelines, to-dos and attachments other than postmortem notebook links.
Synthetics, security signals, RUM and APM.
Dashboards Datadog has marked as deleted.
